newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish year-end inflation at 15.8 pct- Pentor poll.
newsitem.headline: Polish year-end inflation at 15.8 pct- Pentor poll.

text.p: Polish bankers predict December year-on-year inflation to ease to 15.8 percent from 18.5 percent in 1996 and the zloty to be at 3.44, a poll by the private Pentor institute showed.
"According to our poll, year-on-year inflation will be 15.8 percent," Pentor director Eugeniusz Smilowski told a news conference on Tuesday.
Smilowski said 209 bankers polled in June expected the dollar to end the year at 3.44 zlotys, up from 3.40 zlotys in the previous month's forecast.
The bankers also see the Lombard rate rising to 0.3 percent to 24.4 percent at year end.
Credit for enterprises is expected to fall 0.6 percent from its current 23.9 percent and the three-month deposit rate to fall to 16.8 percent, against the current 17.4 percent.
The Pentor survey is commissioned monthly by the Polish Banking Association (ZBP).
